page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.4xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration provides 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.r7se.4xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute tasks, with a PassMark CPU score of 21,177.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,636.0. However, its memory subsystem demonstrates stronger relative performance, achieving a PassMark memory score in the top 25% tier. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 101.82 GB/sec for read operations and 58.78 GB/sec for write operations. For specialized workloads, the server processes 15.01 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a strong text generation speed of 273.35 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter language model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7se.4xlarge offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive CPU scaling. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O must traverse the 6 Gbps network interface. This configuration is suitable for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, data processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.
